chunks: And Sama‘ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام about a woman making up the fasts of the month of Ramadan, and her husband compels her to break the fast. He عليه السلام said: “It is not appropriate for him to compel her after the sun has passed its zenith.”

key_terms.تَقْضِي: she performs the make-up of an obligatory missed act of worship
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s passing the zenith, meaning after midday
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband, in the context of marital authority and limits
key_terms.شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose missed fasts are being made up
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: it is not proper or fitting; an expression indicating disapproval

ai.seo_question: Can a husband force his wife to break a make-up fast of Ramadan after midday?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning a woman who is making up missed fasts of Ramadan and the conduct of her husband toward her during that fast. Imam Abū ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام states that it is not proper for the husband to compel her to break her fast after midday, indicating a legal and marital boundary in relation to qada’ fasting.
